alabama.caution: At least one repair attempt has to fall inside the first year or 12,000 miles, and the summary counts a final try by the manufacturer.

alaska.caution: Days the shop cannot work for reasons outside its control do not count.

arizona.caution: The manufacturer has to have received direct written notice and a chance to repair before the presumption is used.

arkansas.caution: The summary also has a five-attempt path for problems that together substantially impair the car, and a final repair after certified or registered mail.

california.caution: Direct notice is required for the two-repair and four-repair counts only when the warranty or owner's manual clearly told the buyer to send it.

colorado.caution: These counts are the rule for vehicles sold or leased on or after August 7, 2024. The problem has to still be there, and the cure after certified mail counts as one repair.

connecticut.caution: A defect likely to cause death or serious injury uses the express warranty or one year after delivery, and it takes two repairs. Written notice is required only when the warranty or owner's manual says so.

delaware.caution: Use the presumption against the manufacturer only after direct written notice and a chance to fix the car.

florida.caution: A recreational vehicle uses 60 days out of service. Written notice goes out by registered or express mail after 15 days out, and a separate notice after three attempts gives one last repair.

georgia.caution: After the count is met, the manufacturer has 28 days from receiving notice to try one last repair.

hawaii.caution: The manufacturer has to have received a written report and a reasonable chance to repair.

idaho.caution: The single-repair path is a complete brake or steering failure likely to cause death or serious injury. If the problem was first reported during the warranty, attempts within three years of delivery can still count. The four-repair and 30-day paths need written notice and a chance to cure.

illinois.caution: The manufacturer must have received direct written notice and a chance to correct the defect.

indiana.caution: The buyer has to report the problem before the term of protection runs out. If the manufacturer made the disclosure in the statute, the buyer notifies the manufacturer of the claim first.

iowa.caution: Written notice can go out after 20 cumulative days out of service, after three attempts, or after one attempt on a dangerous defect.

kansas.caution: Ten attempts on any problems that substantially impair use and value is a separate path. The counts matter once the manufacturer has actual notice, delivered while the warranty or the one-year period is still open.

kentucky.caution: When a reasonable number of attempts still leaves the car unrepaired, the buyer puts the problem in writing to the manufacturer.

louisiana.caution: If the manufacturer misses the response or repair time in the statute, it loses the right to a final attempt.

maine.caution: The single-repair path is a serious brake or steering failure. The letter asking for a refund or replacement can go out after that failure, and the manufacturer then has seven business days.

maryland.caution: The single-repair path is a brake or steering failure that still will not pass the state safety inspection after a chance to cure. Report the problem by certified mail, return receipt requested.

massachusetts.caution: A business day is a day the authorized dealers' service departments are normally open. The manufacturer gets one more chance of not more than seven business days. The buyer does not have to notify the manufacturer directly before using the state's certified new-car arbitration.

michigan.caution: The four repairs are counted within two years of the first repair attempt. After the third repair, or after 25 days in the shop, written notice by return receipt gives the manufacturer five business days.

minnesota.caution: The single-repair path is a complete brake or steering failure likely to cause death or serious injury. A problem first reported during the warranty can still be supported by attempts within three years of delivery. The four-repair and 30-day routes need written notice and a chance to cure.

mississippi.caution: Routine maintenance is not part of the 15 working days. Write the manufacturer before you rely on the section.

missouri.caution: Days spent on ordinary maintenance stay out of the count. Tell the manufacturer or its agent before the window closes.

montana.caution: Send written notice while the warranty period is still open. The presumption is not used against a manufacturer that never received that notice and a chance to cure.

nebraska.caution: The test is available only once the manufacturer has notice by certified mail and a chance to cure.

nevada.caution: Report the problem in writing before the express warranty ends or one year after delivery, whichever is earlier. The 30-day count can run longer when the repair is delayed for reasons outside the manufacturer's or dealer's control.

new-hampshire.caution: The presumption is measured during the express warranty. A car the owner can use for a major part of the day is not out of service. After the third repair or the 30 business days, written notice gives the manufacturer one final chance.

new-jersey.caution: A motorhome uses 45 calendar days out of service where a passenger car uses 20. The presumption applies only after certified-mail notice and one chance to repair within 10 calendar days.

new-mexico.caution: Routine maintenance is not counted. Direct written notice and a chance to cure have to come first.

new-york.caution: Report the problem to the manufacturer, its agent, or an authorized dealer. Motor homes in the same section follow a different path.

north-carolina.caution: The 20 business days are counted during any 12-month period of the warranty. Notify the manufacturer in writing and allow up to 15 calendar days to correct the problem, unless it never disclosed that written notice was required.

north-dakota.caution: More than three repairs means a fourth visit while the trouble is still present. The presumption does not run until the manufacturer has had direct notice and a chance to cure.

ohio.caution: Eight attempts to repair any problems is a separate path. Report the nonconformity to the manufacturer, its agent, or its authorized dealer during that year or 18,000 miles.

oklahoma.caution: Without written notice during the warranty or that year, and a chance to cure, the presumption does not apply.

oregon.caution: A motor home uses 60 days out of service. The manufacturer needs a direct letter and a chance to correct the defect before the presumption is used.

pennsylvania.caution: A motorcycle uses one year or the warranty, and the statute does not add a mileage cap for motorcycles. When the car comes back to the same dealer a second time, the dealer notifies the manufacturer.

rhode-island.caution: Report the nonconformity during the term of protection. The manufacturer also gets one more cure of not more than seven calendar days once it knows the four-repair or 30-day limit has been met.

south-carolina.caution: The summary asks for a report within the first 12 months or 12,000 miles. The presumption counts repairs and days during the express warranty. Written notice is required when the manufacturer clearly said so at the sale.

south-dakota.caution: The problem has to start during the first year or 12,000 miles. Repairs that count can run out to 24 months or 24,000 miles if one attempt happened during that rights period.

tennessee.caution: Send certified mail before you go further. If the presumption is already met, the manufacturer gets one more chance of not more than ten days.

texas.caution: The two-repair path is only a serious safety hazard. The 30-day path is its own test: a nonconformity that still substantially impairs use or market value after 30 or more cumulative days. Days a comparable loaner is provided do not count. Subsection (b) extends the periods for war, invasion, strike, fire, flood, or another natural disaster. A refund or replacement order needs written notice and a chance to cure.

utah.caution: Tell the manufacturer, its agent, or its authorized dealer during the warranty or during that same year.

vermont.caution: At least the first repair attempt has to happen while the express warranty is still in effect. A car the owner can still drive for most of the day is not treated as out of service. After a reasonable attempt or 30 days, notify the manufacturer in writing.

virginia.caution: The rights period can run longer if the manufacturer was notified and the problem is still unrepaired at the end. A serious safety defect is a life-threatening malfunction that interferes with ordinary control or creates a risk of fire or explosion. If the presumption is already met, the manufacturer gets up to 15 more days, and the warranty or owner's manual has to disclose that written notice is required.

washington.caution: For a car that is not a motor home, two or more different serious safety defects each repaired once in a 12-month period is a separate path, and at least 15 of the 30 days out of service have to fall during the written warranty. A motor home uses different counts. Make a written request before a replacement or repurchase.

west-virginia.caution: The presumption stops at the end of the express warranty or one year after delivery, whichever is sooner. A different repair-duty clock runs for the longer of those two periods. The counts apply only after written notice and at least one chance to cure.

wisconsin.caution: Time lost to a flood, other natural disaster, war, invasion, fire, or strike does not count. A car the owner is still driving counts as out of service only when a problem substantially affects use or safety and has already had at least two repair attempts.

wyoming.caution: More than three repairs of the same problem is the repair path. During that year, tell the manufacturer, its agent, or the dealer authorized to do the repair. The refund or replacement remedy is withheld if the owner has not finished a manufacturer's informal dispute program that meets federal rules.

washington-dc.caution: The 30 days can be extended for a war, invasion, strike, fire, flood, or similar disaster. While the window is open, tell the manufacturer, an agent, or an authorized dealer. A lawsuit waits until the claim has been submitted to the Board of Consumer Claims Arbitration.
